organizational_logic: Modular mid-level concepts and domain extensions organize classes and relationships in Earth system science.
inclusion_basis: Provides practically reusable concept systems and ontology modules for environmental research.
boundary_note: The entire suite counts as one candidate; its roughly several hundred modules are not split into independent KOS.

organizational_logic: Organizes distinguishable features, properties, and phenotypic traits of developing or mature plants.
inclusion_basis: An independent namespace and ontology for plant traits, organizing different objects from PO.
boundary_note: Can work with PO but is neither its format nor its version; counted separately.

organizational_logic: Cross-species anatomical structures are organized through shared class hierarchies and ontological relationships that can bridge species-specific structures.
inclusion_basis: Covers cross-species anatomical categories, distinct from a single-species name list.
boundary_note: Basic, Simple, Base, Full, and the formats are only release variants.

subject_domain: Conceptual modeling; objects; events; social entities
organizational_logic: Objects, events, and social entities are organized in layers, including microtheories of types, roles, and part-whole relationships.
inclusion_basis: Covers types and relationships in conceptual modeling and has a lightweight OWL implementation.
boundary_note: The different layers and gUFO are counted together as one lineage.

organizational_logic: Organizes units by measured quantity and unit category, for reference by ontologies such as those for phenotypic qualities.
inclusion_basis: The OBO entry and repository provide an independent ontology of unit concepts, allowing comparison of specialized measurement organization.
boundary_note: Its goals overlap with QUDT, but it is maintained independently; the repository states that maintenance relies mainly on the community and does not claim dedicated full-time maintenance.

subject_domain: Researchers, organizations, scholarly activities, outputs, funding
organizational_logic: Represents scholarly activity networks through relationships among entities such as people, organizations, outputs, roles, activities, and funding.
inclusion_basis: The VIVO-ISF lead in the SPAR paper was traced to the official ontology, adding a semantic schema for research activities.
boundary_note: Only the VIVO content ontology is counted; the VIVO software, institutional installations, and historical VIVO-ISF name are not counted separately.

resource_name: Yet Another More Advanced Top-level Ontology
organizational_logic: Uses formalized foundational concepts and relationships to address upper-ontology modeling issues.
inclusion_basis: Original-author papers on the upper ontology and public resources are available, supporting its inclusion in foundational ontology comparisons.
boundary_note: Identified at the candidate level, without a commitment to formal quality scoring in this round. The early author manuscript and the formal 2022 paper have different bibliographic records; the placeholder year in the earlier manuscript's header was not treated as the publication year.
source_title: YAMATO: Yet Another More Advanced Top-level Ontology

subtype: Entity knowledge graph extracted from an encyclopedia
organizational_logic: Entity fact triples are linked to a cross-domain class hierarchy; classes can have multiple parents
inclusion_basis: Existing core system; enables comparison of automatically extracted data and an explicit ontology schema
related_resources: Derived from Wikipedia and integrates Wikidata; DBpedia Ontology is recorded as its schema without double-counting
boundary_note: The class hierarchy is not a single tree

organizational_logic: Connects entities through entity IDs, types, property statements, and qualifiers; class/instance associations are expressed through relationships
inclusion_basis: Existing core system; represents a collaboratively maintained graph of entities and facts
secondary_attributes: F3: Includes class and property schemas; F5: Includes a lexeme module
related_resources: Independent project; can be aggregated by YAGO, DBpedia, and others
boundary_note: The lexeme module is not counted as a separate KOS

organizational_logic: Entities and facts are constrained by class hierarchies; integrated sources vary by version
inclusion_basis: Existing core system; represents an encyclopedic knowledge base with integrated schemas and cleaned data
related_resources: 4.6 is based on Wikidata; earlier versions used WordNet, Wikipedia, GeoNames, and other sources
boundary_note: Versions are combined into one item; YAGO and Wikidata cannot be treated as fully independent data sources
source_title: Download data, code, and logo of Yago projects

organizational_logic: Cultural objects and catalog records use modular ontologies to express types, places, events, and contextual relationships
inclusion_basis: Represents the conversion of institutional catalogs into domain knowledge graphs through ontologies
related_resources: Data comes from the General Catalogue of Italian Cultural Heritage; reuses Cultural-ON, OntoPiA, and others
boundary_note: Ontology modules and the graph are combined as one system; each version/module is not treated as an independent system

resource_name: Activities, States, Events, and their Relations
organizational_logic: Dependency patterns extract event nodes; discourse relations such as Result form edges; includes a conceptualization layer
inclusion_basis: Represents organization through event relations and conceptualization, broadening graph structures beyond entity graphs
boundary_note: Not a purely factual database standardized by human curation; extraction confidence and relation semantics require later consideration
source_title: ASER (Activities, States, Events, and their Relations)

subtype: Event and social commonsense relation graph
organizational_logic: Uses events or phrases as nodes and typed relations to represent inferential knowledge such as intentions, preconditions, and effects
inclusion_basis: Adds knowledge organization centered on event inference rather than class trees
related_resources: Different versions are combined; integrated into CSKG
boundary_note: COMET is a related generative model and is not counted as another KOS; machine-generated outputs cannot be treated as original graph facts
source_title: (Comet-) Atomic 2020: On Symbolic and Neural Commonsense Knowledge Graphs

organizational_logic: Shared URIs and property vocabularies convert entities and relationships from different databases to RDF and interlink them
inclusion_basis: Represents knowledge organization through cross-source URIs and vocabulary mappings
related_resources: Aggregates multiple biological and chemical databases; does not independently produce all facts
boundary_note: Counted as one data integration system; download mirrors/endpoints are not counted repeatedly

organizational_logic: Specific cultural objects are organized by authorized names, work types, hierarchies, and links to creators/places/subjects
inclusion_basis: Adds resources for work entities, distinct from AAT's generic concepts
secondary_attributes: F2: Name authority and thesaurus relationships
related_resources: Getty series; links to AAT, ULAN, TGN, and IA
boundary_note: Current service and data status are separately flagged for later accessibility assessment; online browsing is not assumed to imply full download availability
source_title: Getty Vocabularies Update: IA and CONA

organizational_logic: Word/phrase nodes are connected by typed edges such as IsA, PartOf, and UsedFor
inclusion_basis: Represents a commonsense concept relation graph for comparison with named entity graphs
related_resources: Integrates Open Mind Common Sense, Wiktionary, WordNet, DBpedia, and other sources
boundary_note: Not a pure entity fact graph; minor versions are combined

organizational_logic: Uses a hyper-relational graph model to unify word senses, concepts, and commonsense edges
inclusion_basis: Represents integration of multiple KOS and cross-schema alignment
related_resources: Integrates ATOMIC, ConceptNet, FrameNet, Roget, Visual Genome, Wikidata, and WordNet
boundary_note: An independent integration project, but not an evidence source independent of its seven upstream sources

organizational_logic: Entities and 107 relation types integrate multiple databases; a relation glossary records semantics and provenance
inclusion_basis: Represents an integrated domain graph with an explicit relation vocabulary and provenance
related_resources: Integrates DrugBank, Hetionet, GNBR, STRING, IntAct, DGIdb, and the literature
boundary_note: An aggregated resource; retains distinctions in source licenses and provenance

organizational_logic: Events, participants, places, and temporal relations use a unified RDF schema
inclusion_basis: Represents organization through events and temporal relations, distinct from entity attribute graphs
related_resources: Integrates event information from Wikidata, DBpedia, YAGO, and Wikipedia
boundary_note: The graph is independently integrated, but its original factual sources are not independent
source_title: A Multilingual Event-Centric Temporal Knowledge Graph

organizational_logic: Typed entities and property facts, with RDF triples and schema snapshots
inclusion_basis: A historically significant resource, adding to the development trajectory of entity knowledge graphs
related_resources: Has mappings to Wikidata; some machine learning benchmarks derive from its subsets
boundary_note: Maintenance and API services have ended; included only as a historical candidate, not a current system

organizational_logic: Geographic entities have feature types, administrative parents, countries, proximity, and location relationships
inclusion_basis: Represents organization of global geographical name entities by type and administrative hierarchy
related_resources: Supplies geographic entities to multiple knowledge graphs; its ontology schema is not counted separately
boundary_note: Geographic containment must be distinguished from genus-species hierarchies

subtype: Authority for named subjects and fictional entities
organizational_logic: Named events, figures, narratives, and subjects have equivalence, hierarchical, and associative relationships
inclusion_basis: Adds organizational structures for cultural subjects and fictional entities
secondary_attributes: F2: Officially defined as a thesaurus
related_resources: Getty series; complements AAT, TGN, ULAN, and CONA
boundary_note: Distinct from the Iconclass classification; retains a cross-reference explanation

organizational_logic: Organizes subjects, people, organizations, events, places, and works using authority identifiers and names.
inclusion_basis: Public institutional documentation clearly identifies the resource and its organizational structure, adding a domain or organizational approach to this group.
boundary_note: The integrated authority file contains subject concepts and entities; assigned consistently to F4 by its principal objects, alongside TGN/ULAN/VIAF, with a cross-reference to F2. Former SWD/PND/GKD files are no longer counted separately.

organizational_logic: Entity IDs and schema.org types; the public search API returns only matching entities
inclusion_basis: Records an influential KG with limited openness, avoiding the misrepresentation of searchability as full reusability
related_resources: Related to resources such as open encyclopedias; the complete upstream source list is uncertain in this round
boundary_note: Restricted candidate: the public API does not provide the complete graph of inter-entity relationships and is unsuitable as directly downloadable comparison data

subtype: Biomedical graph with multiple relation types
organizational_logic: Multiple node and relation types connect diseases, drugs, genes, and biological processes
inclusion_basis: Represents a biomedical heterogeneous graph with explicit types
secondary_attributes: F3: Node and relation type schema
related_resources: Integrates biomedical sources; reused by DRKG and others
boundary_note: Original sources and downstream aggregated graphs do not constitute statistically independent samples
source_title: Hetionet: an integrative network of disease

subtype: Integrated graph of reference concepts and entity types
organizational_logic: Reference concepts form a type system under the KKO upper structure, mapping entities, properties, and external vocabularies
inclusion_basis: Represents an upper ontology organizing entity types and concepts from multiple sources
related_resources: Integrates Wikipedia, Wikidata, schema.org, DBpedia, GeoNames, OpenCyc, and UNSPSC
boundary_note: KKO and KBpedia are recorded together to avoid counting the same system's schema and instances twice
source_title: How to Use the Knowledge Graph

subtype: Cross-domain geographic and environmental knowledge graph
subject_domain: Geography; environment; disasters; agriculture; public health
organizational_logic: Connects data across domains through typed objects, spatiotemporal relations, observations, and provenance
inclusion_basis: Directly connected to CLeAR's environmental research context, demonstrating cross-domain data integration
secondary_attributes: F3: Ontology schemas such as GeoSPARQL and SOSA
related_resources: Aggregates environmental and social data and links to Wikidata, GNIS, and others; its own ontology is not counted separately
boundary_note: Not all nodes form parent-child trees; spatial containment, observations, and event causality must be distinguished

organizational_logic: OSM tags map to RDF resources, types, and properties; places link to geometric objects and external entities
inclusion_basis: Represents geographic semantic data based on explicit mappings
related_resources: Derived from OpenStreetMap; shares the original map source with WorldKG but uses different modeling
boundary_note: The system is combined into one item; counts do not reflect the number of OSM download copies

organizational_logic: Genes, diseases, and phenotypes are connected through Biolink semantic relationships and ontology identifiers
inclusion_basis: Represents cross-species phenotype integration, distinct from a single classification ontology
related_resources: Integrates multiple gene/disease/phenotype resources; HPO/MONDO are related sources rather than the same resource
boundary_note: Web pages, APIs, and Neo4j are access channels to the same graph and are not counted separately

organizational_logic: Categories, binary relations, and confidence scores organize facts learned from web pages
inclusion_basis: Represents automatically extracted knowledge organization with confidence scores
secondary_attributes: F3: Seed ontology and relation constraints
related_resources: Related to web extraction corpora; the learning algorithm and knowledge base must be distinguished
boundary_note: Historical research resource; no claim of ongoing updates is made in this round

organizational_logic: Research products, people, organizations, projects, and data sources are connected through semantic relationships
inclusion_basis: Adds relationship organization at the research activity level, distinct from conceptual graphs of research content
related_resources: Aggregates metadata from research data sources; may share records with other bibliographic graphs
boundary_note: Borderline candidate: primarily a research metadata graph; resource scale cannot substitute for the semantic richness of a KOS

organizational_logic: Uses templates and semantic properties to organize research contributions, problems, methods, results, and comparable content
inclusion_basis: Represents semantic structuring of paper content, distinguishing it from graphs containing only bibliographic metadata
related_resources: Built jointly by researchers and extraction processes; not a collection of full-text original papers
boundary_note: The online platform is an access channel; the candidate is its structured research knowledge resource

subtype: Historical geographic entity authority and relationship database
organizational_logic: Distinguishes places, names, locations, and connections; relationships can express part-whole, network, temporal, and other semantics
inclusion_basis: Represents historical geographic knowledge organization with evidence and temporal qualifications
secondary_attributes: F2: Geographical name authorities; F3: Place relationship model
related_resources: Can interlink with other geographic and cultural heritage resources
boundary_note: Not an ordinary unstructured list of geographical names; uncertainty in historical locations must be retained

organizational_logic: Diseases connect to genes, drugs, phenotypes, anatomy, and biological processes; relations distinguish indications, contraindications, and other meanings
inclusion_basis: Represents a disease-centric knowledge graph with diverse medical relation semantics
related_resources: Integrates 20 resources and ontologies; shares upstream sources with other biomedical graphs
boundary_note: Not a disease classification; edges between different node types generally are not parent-child relations

subtype: Probabilistic classification graph of concepts and instances
organizational_logic: Extracts concept-subconcept and concept-instance isA relations from text, represented with probabilities/typicality
inclusion_basis: Represents a borderline type combining probabilistic concept classification and instance relations
secondary_attributes: F1: Probabilistic taxonomy; F5: Word conceptualization
related_resources: Probase was subsequently released as Microsoft Concept Graph; used for ASER conceptualization
boundary_note: Not a pure named entity fact graph; the two names are combined without double-counting

resource_name: Scalable Precision Medicine Open Knowledge Engine
organizational_logic: Connects nodes for genetics, proteins, tissues, organs, phenotypes, the environment, and other areas through multiple relation types
inclusion_basis: Adds a specialized graph linking clinical and basic biomedical knowledge
secondary_attributes: F3: Entity types and edge semantics
related_resources: Integrates LINCS, GWAS Catalog, ChEMBL, DrugBank, and other sources
boundary_note: Access/authorization remains to be assessed; private clinical data is not equated with the public graph
source_title: Scalable Precision Medicine Open Knowledge Engine

organizational_logic: Geographical name entities are placed in geographic whole-part and administrative hierarchies, supporting multiple parent places and historical contexts
inclusion_basis: Demonstrates geographic hierarchies in an entity authority, distinct from conceptual genus-species hierarchies
secondary_attributes: F2: Officially designed as a thesaurus
related_resources: Getty vocabulary series; interlinked with AAT, ULAN, CONA, and IA
boundary_note: Primary placement in F4 is this study's analytical grouping; the official thesaurus type should not be erased

organizational_logic: Name equivalence, instance classification, and organizational whole-part hierarchies; kinship between people is represented by associative edges
inclusion_basis: Clearly demonstrates that is-a, instance-of, and part-of cannot be treated as a single parent-child relationship
related_resources: Getty series, interlinked with AAT, TGN, CONA, and IA
boundary_note: Personal genealogies cannot be treated as ULAN's primary hierarchy

organizational_logic: Clusters multilingual name authority records for the same entity, retaining original records and cross-references
inclusion_basis: Represents entity identity and authority name linking, without requiring every system to have a parent-child tree
related_resources: Aggregates authority files from multiple countries and institutions; its data is not independent of those sources
boundary_note: The main structure is entity alignment and authority references, not a general subject classification tree

organizational_logic: Maps OSM entities to geographic classes and properties and connects spatial objects
inclusion_basis: Represents a domain graph formed by semantically structuring map data
related_resources: Extracted from OpenStreetMap, linking to DBpedia/Wikidata categories
boundary_note: The WorldKG ontology and graph are combined into one item; OSM mirrors are not listed repeatedly as independent KOS

subtype: Multilingual word-sense and encyclopedic semantic network
organizational_logic: Multilingual synonyms form synsets; concepts and named entities are connected through semantic relations
inclusion_basis: Existing core system; connects lexical-semantic and encyclopedic entity structures
secondary_attributes: F4: Includes named entities and encyclopedic knowledge
related_resources: Integrates WordNet, Open English WordNet, Wikipedia, and other sources
boundary_note: Different versions are combined; third-party research subsets are not counted as new KOS

organizational_logic: Lexical units evoke semantic frames containing roles; frames form a network through inheritance and other relations
inclusion_basis: Represents the logic of organizing word senses through scenario frames
related_resources: FrameNets for different languages are noted as related implementations, not counted separately by language; reused by UBY and CSKG
boundary_note: The official website has moved; FrameBase is a derived ontology, not the same resource

subtype: Lexical knowledge base based on sememe composition
organizational_logic: Word senses are represented by combinations of a finite set of sememes and sememe roles, expandable into sememe trees with queryable inter-sememe relations
inclusion_basis: Represents meaning decomposition and composition, distinct from merely linking whole word-sense nodes
secondary_attributes: F3: Sememe concepts and their relations
related_resources: OpenHowNet provides open data/APIs based on HowNet; combined into one item
boundary_note: Not to be confused with China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI); the API software is not another KOS

organizational_logic: Word or word-sense nodes connect through multiple edge types, including synonymy, antonymy, hypernymy/hyponymy, part-whole, and agent relations
inclusion_basis: Represents a typed lexical network crowdsourced by an independent language community
secondary_attributes: F4: Includes commonsense and role relations
related_resources: Can link to external resources such as WordNet and UMLS; not a translated language version of WordNet
boundary_note: The game is the collection method; the candidate is the rezoJDM knowledge resource

subtype: Lexicon of noun senses and argument roles
organizational_logic: Each noun sense contains an argument roleset, aligned with corresponding verb roles where possible
inclusion_basis: Adds noun argument structure, distinct from purely hypernymic/hyponymic noun classification
related_resources: Derived from NOMLEX and coordinated with PropBank; some frames directly reuse PropBank
boundary_note: Only the frame lexicon and noun role definitions are included; annotated Penn Treebank texts do not count as a new KOS

subtype: Lexicon of verb patterns and semantic types
organizational_logic: Verb usage patterns contain argument structures whose arguments are constrained by the CPA semantic type ontology
inclusion_basis: Represents organization of word senses through contextual patterns and argument types
related_resources: Patterns derive from corpus analysis; CPA semantic types are recorded within this entry without double-counting
boundary_note: Only the pattern lexicon and type structure are included; the BNC corpus is not treated as a KOS
source_title: Automatic classification of patterns from the Pattern Dictionary of English Verbs

subtype: Lexicon of predicate senses and argument roles
organizational_logic: Each predicate sense corresponds to a roleset and local role definitions; not a unified parent-child tree
inclusion_basis: Adds flat roleset organization to avoid forcing all KOS into classification trees
secondary_attributes: No fixed cross-group assignment; a lexical resource for semantic annotation
related_resources: Has mappings to VerbNet and FrameNet; NomBank shares some frames
boundary_note: Only the independent frame lexicon is included; annotated corpora and the AMR formal language are not counted together as KOS

organizational_logic: Words are organized by broad conceptual classes, sections, and heads, then grouped by part of speech and meaning
inclusion_basis: Represents a traditional lexical system classified by meaning, distinct from a thesaurus for indexing document subjects
secondary_attributes: F1: Concept classification; F2: Thesaurus in the broad sense
related_resources: Used by CSKG and others; print editions and digital mirrors are combined
boundary_note: Structures/licenses vary across editions; citations must specify the edition, as this is not a fixed current standard
source_title: Roget's Thesaurus: a Lexical Resource to Treasure

resource_name: UBY: A Large-scale Unified Lexical-Semantic Resource
subtype: Multiresource word-sense alignment and integration database
organizational_logic: Uses LMF to unify lexical entries, word senses, and cross-resource correspondences
inclusion_basis: Represents structural unification and alignment among lexical KOS
related_resources: Integrates WordNet, Wiktionary, FrameNet, VerbNet, and other sources; some versions can support GermaNet
boundary_note: An aggregated resource is not an independent source of original word senses; LMF is a standard and is not separately counted in this entry
source_title: UBY: A Large-scale Unified Lexical-Semantic Resource

resource_name: UCREL Semantic Analysis System Semantic Tagset
subtype: Classification system of semantic fields for word senses
organizational_logic: Subdivides 21 major semantic domains hierarchically; tags group related word senses
inclusion_basis: Represents a hierarchical category system for annotating lexical meanings
related_resources: Initially based on the Longman Lexicon; language-specific taggers use the same system
boundary_note: The candidate comprises semantic tags and lexical mappings; USAS/Wmatrix software is not treated as a KOS

subtype: Verb-sense frames and universal role inventory
organizational_logic: Groups WordNet verb synsets into semantically coherent frames using cross-frame roles and selectional preferences
inclusion_basis: Represents an organizational approach that adds frames and universal argument structures on top of WordNet
related_resources: Built on WordNet and linked to BabelNet; adds manually created frame structures
boundary_note: A derived and enhanced resource, not a corpus source wholly independent of WordNet
source_title: VerbAtlas: a Novel Large-Scale Verbal Semantic Resource and Its Application to Semantic Role Labeling

subtype: Verb class hierarchy and argument structure lexicon
organizational_logic: Organizes verb classes by shared syntactic-semantic behavior; subclasses inherit parent-class frames and role restrictions
inclusion_basis: Represents verb category structures with explicit inheritance
secondary_attributes: F1: Class hierarchy; F3: Role constraints
related_resources: Mapped to WordNet, PropBank, and FrameNet; versions are combined
boundary_note: Not all verbs belong to one purely semantic tree; classes are based on syntactic and semantic commonalities

subtype: Collaborative dictionary and word-sense relation database
organizational_logic: Entries and sense descriptions connect synonymy, antonymy, hypernymy/hyponymy, and other semantic relations
inclusion_basis: Represents collaborative dictionary organization for comparison with synset and sememe models
related_resources: DBnary extracts from Wiktionary in different languages; multilingual sites are combined as one system; DBnary: https://github.com/serasset/dbnary/blob/master/README.md?plain=1
boundary_note: Boundary: not every entry has a complete relation structure; ordinary plain-text dictionaries cannot all be included indiscriminately. DBnary is a structured extraction derived from Wiktionary, recorded as a related resource within this entry without increasing the candidate count.

resource_name: WordNet family (Princeton WordNet and related editions)
subtype: Network of synonym sets and word-sense relations
organizational_logic: Word senses are organized into synsets, using relations such as hypernymy/hyponymy, part-whole, antonymy, and entailment
inclusion_basis: Represents the classic organizational logic based on word-sense relations
secondary_attributes: F3: Can function as a lightweight lexical ontology
related_resources: Open English Wordnet derives from Princeton WordNet; multilingual WordNets and mappings are related implementations
boundary_note: Grouped by system family in this round, without inflating counts by individual languages/versions; project maintenance status varies
